title: We have many examples in our periphery where heat is (part 2)
source: neb-class-11-physics — We have many examples in our periphery where heat is, pages 276-277 [neb-class-11-physics-book.pdf]
textbookText: Sample Questions: 1. When water is placed in an ice-cube tray in a freezer, why does the water not freeze all at once when the temperature has reached the freezing point? In fact, the water freezes first in the layer adjacent to the sides of the tray, why? 2. Why is snow abetter heat-insulator than ice? 3. A plank of wood lying in the sun absorbs more heat than a shiny metal does. But the wood feels less hot than the metal when you pick it up. Explain. 4. You are requested to sit on a chair at a wedding party in a cold winter evening. Would you like to choose a metal chair or a wooden chair? 5. Why does a piece of paper wrapped tightly on a wooden rod burn more quickly when held over a flame than a similar piece wrapped on a metal rod?
